pull.title: MINOR: Avoid per-record leader epoch `Optional` allocation in `CompletedFetch` and `ShareCompletedFetch`
pull.body:
`CompletedFetch#fetchRecords` and `ShareCompletedFetch#fetchRecords`
built a new `Optional<Integer>` for the leader epoch for every returned
record, although the value only changes per batch. Each `ConsumerRecord`
keeps a reference to it, so escape analysis cannot remove it: 16 bytes
per record, or 32 bytes when the epoch is above 127 and the `Integer`
has to be boxed.

`CompletedFetch` already computes this value once per batch into
`lastEpoch`, so pass that to `parseRecord`. `ShareCompletedFetch` now
computes it once per batch into the new `currentBatchLeaderEpoch` field
when it advances `currentBatch`. `Optional` is immutable, so sharing one
instance between the records of a batch does not change observable
behaviour.

Results of the new `CompletedFetchBenchmark` (500 records in 5 batches,
`-f 3 -wi 5 -i 5 -prof gc`, JDK 21, errors are 99.9% CIs):

```text
epoch  before (us/op)   after (us/op)   gc.alloc.rate.norm (B/op)
5      54.216 ± 11.531  47.118 ± 2.025  216,096 -> 208,096 (-3.7%)
1000   49.508 ±  1.252  46.757 ± 1.745  224,176 -> 208,176 (-7.1%)
```

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue_comments.body:
Thanks in advance for taking a look!

- `CompletedFetch` is package-private, so `CompletedFetchBenchmark` reaches its constructor and `fetchRecords` through `MethodHandle`s resolved once in `@Setup`. Happy to drop or restructure it.
- Time is only significant for epoch `1000` (−5.6 %, non-overlapping CIs); epoch `5` was a noisy baseline run on a shared VM. The allocation drop is exact for both.
- New `testLeaderEpochIsSetPerBatch` in `CompletedFetchTest` and `ShareCompletedFetchTest` uses epochs `5` / `NO_PARTITION_LEADER_EPOCH` / `1000` and reads 2 records per `fetchRecords` call, so reads resume mid-batch. Both tests pass on trunk and on this branch.
- `./gradlew clients:test --tests 'org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.*'` passes (3,245 tests).
- `./gradlew clients:clients-integration-tests:test --tests ConsumerIntegrationTest` passes (14 tests, incl. `testLeaderEpoch`).
- `checkstyleMain`, `checkstyleTest`, `spotlessCheck` and `spotbugsMain` pass for `clients` and `jmh-benchmarks`.

commit.message:
MINOR: Avoid allocating the leader epoch Optional per record in CompletedFetch and ShareCompletedFetch

CompletedFetch#fetchRecords and ShareCompletedFetch#fetchRecords called
maybeLeaderEpoch(currentBatch.partitionLeaderEpoch()) for every returned
record, allocating a new Optional (and a boxed Integer for epochs > 127)
per record, although the value only changes per batch. CompletedFetch
already computes exactly this value once per batch into lastEpoch.

Reuse the per-batch Optional instead: CompletedFetch passes lastEpoch,
ShareCompletedFetch computes it once when it advances to the next batch.
Optional is immutable, so sharing one instance between the records of a
batch does not change observable behaviour.

CompletedFetchBenchmark (500 records, 5 batches) shows 16 B/record less
allocation for small epochs and 32 B/record for epochs > 127.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MTr23v7v98uREoAwefLXGP
